body:
It's really hard to reproduce, seems it could be some kind of a race condition. I haven't been able to reproduce it in any way other than just editing my project and then it happens randomly. I'm gonna still keep running gdb, just installed debug symbols for libdecor as well to get some more info on what's happening. 

Also let me know if you need any more info about the crash and how I could provide it.

Hi, thank you for your report!

This feels like an edge case in the GTK lidecor plugin, maybe related to our custom game embedding layer.

Could you please let me know the compositor you're using, including its version? I'd be also interested in seeing what `wayland-info` (from [`wayland-utils`](https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/resolute/+package/wayland-utils)) returns on your computer.

> I'm gonna keep running gdb still, just installed debug symbols for libdecor as well to get some more info on what's happening.

That's great! Please let me know when you manage to get a backtrace from that :D

> the compositor you're using, including its version?

I'm running gnome 46.0, mutter 46.2-1ubuntu0.24.04.13.

> Could you please let me know the compositor you're using, including its version? I'd be also interested in seeing what wayland-info (from [wayland-utils](https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/resolute/+package/wayland-utils)) returns on your computer.

Update: at 8 hours now :smile:

The gdb backtrace shows that the crash happens in `libdecor-gtk.so`, so this is probably a libdecor bug and not something we can fix in Godot.

Which version of libdecor do you have? I think Ubuntu 24.04 might be on 0.2.2 (even 25.10 is still on 0.2.2 so upgrading wouldn't help).

Ideally, you'd try to upgrade to the latest 0.2.5 and see if the bug is still reproducible. But I recognize that it's not trivial when using distro packages. You'd have to compile libdecor from source and install it system wide (after uninstalling the Ubuntu package), or if you're familiar with deb packaging, make your own package for version 0.2.5 from Ubuntu's `debian` files. If it's still reproducible in libdecor 0.2.5, then it should be reported upstream to https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/libdecor/libdecor

With the latest Godot version from `master` (was added recently, not sure if it's in beta2 already), you can set the `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_LIBDECOR` environment variable to disable libdecor. You will lose window decorations in Wayland for Godot, but that might solve this crash.

Sorry was on vacation. This has not been happening for a long while, so you're correct to set this as non-blocking. But it's interesting, as it originally happened 3 times in a short timespan which got me to create this issue.

I'll keep running my project in gdb and will report if it crashes again but not a big issue by any means I think.

> Which version of libdecor do you have? I think Ubuntu 24.04 might be on 0.2.2 

Yes 0.2.2. I'll see what I can do.
